marks.reason: S1 attributes the notice to Musk’s buyer group and describes it as an attempt to exercise a contractual termination right, not proof that the deal ended.
S1 identifies the alleged failure to provide requested fake- or spam-account data and presents it as the buyer group’s allegation.
S2 attributes to Twitter both its rejection of the notice as invalid and its denial that it breached the agreement.
S2 gives USD 54.20 per share as the price at which Twitter sought to enforce closing, not as a realized payment or return.
S2 identifies the board’s plan to seek enforcement and Twitter’s reservation of its specific-performance right, without suggesting that a court had granted relief.
S1 and S2 distinguish the buyer’s notice from an uncontested termination and explain that neither termination nor closing was established at the cutoff.
